description: Na₂Ge₂S₅ crystallizes in the orthorhombic Cmcm space group. There are two inequivalent Na¹⁺ sites. In the first Na¹⁺ site, Na¹⁺ is bonded in a 6-coordinate geometry to six S²⁻ atoms. There are a spread of Na-S bond distances ranging from 2.94-3.35 Å. In the second Na¹⁺ site, Na¹⁺ is bonded to six S²⁻ atoms to form distorted NaS₆ octahedra that share corners with two equivalent NaS₆ octahedra, corners with four equivalent GeS₄ tetrahedra,  an edgeedge with one NaS₆ octahedra, and edges with two equivalent GeS₄ tetrahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles are 47°. There are a spread of Na-S bond distances ranging from 2.88-3.37 Å. There are two inequivalent Ge⁴⁺ sites. In the first Ge⁴⁺ site, Ge⁴⁺ is bonded to four S²⁻ atoms to form GeS₄ tetrahedra that share corners with three GeS₄ tetrahedra and edges with two equivalent NaS₆ octahedra. There are a spread of Ge-S bond distances ranging from 2.13-2.25 Å. In the second Ge⁴⁺ site, Ge⁴⁺ is bonded to four S²⁻ atoms to form GeS₄ tetrahedra that share corners with four equivalent NaS₆ octahedra and corners with three GeS₄ tetrahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 14-80°. There are a spread of Ge-S bond distances ranging from 2.15-2.25 Å. There are five inequivalent S²⁻ sites. In the first S²⁻ site, S²⁻ is bonded in a distorted rectangular see-saw-like geometry to two equivalent Na¹⁺ and two equivalent Ge⁴⁺ atoms. In the second S²⁻ site, S²⁻ is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to two Na¹⁺ and two Ge⁴⁺ atoms. In the third S²⁻ site, S²⁻ is bonded in a water-like geometry to two equivalent Ge⁴⁺ atoms. In the fourth S²⁻ site, S²⁻ is bonded to four Na¹⁺ and one Ge⁴⁺ atom to form distorted SNa₄Ge square pyramids that share corners with six equivalent SNa₃Ge trigonal pyramids and edges with two equivalent SNa₄Ge square pyramids. In the fifth S²⁻ site, S²⁻ is bonded to three Na¹⁺ and one Ge⁴⁺ atom to form distorted SNa₃Ge trigonal pyramids that share corners with six equivalent SNa₄Ge square pyramids and corners with two equivalent SNa₃Ge trigonal pyramids.
